title: Affine criterion for schematic density of finitely many principal opens
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative ring [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and $f_1,\ldots,f_n\in A$, with $n\geq0$. Write $A_{f_i}=A[1/f_i]$ [def-weil-ring-localization-away] and $D(f_i)=\{\mathfrak p\in\operatorname{Spec}A:f_i\notin\mathfrak p\}$. Put $U=\bigcup_i D(f_i)\subseteq\operatorname{Spec}A$. The natural map $A\to\bigoplus_i A_{f_i}$ is injective if and only if $A\to A^{\oplus n}$, $a\mapsto(f_1a,\ldots,f_na)$, is injective. For the open immersion $j:U\hookrightarrow\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-open-immersion], these conditions are also equivalent to injectivity of the natural restriction map of sheaves $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\to j_*\mathcal O_U$.

proof.text: Write $\lambda(a)=(a/1)_i$ and $\mu(a)=(f_i a)_i$. By [def-weil-ring-localization-away], $\lambda(a)=0$ precisely when each $f_i^{e_i}a=0$ for some $e_i\geq1$ (increase a zero exponent to one). If $\mu(a)=0$, then $f_i a=0$ for every $i$; choosing all $e_i=1$ gives $\lambda(a)=0$. Injectivity of $\lambda$ therefore gives $a=0$, proving injectivity of $\mu$ by subtraction. Conversely, if $\mu$ is injective, apply [lem-trf-finite-scalar-power-common-kernel] with $M=A$ and scalar action $b\cdot a=ba$ to these exponents to obtain $a=0$ whenever $\lambda(a)=0$. For both additive maps, zero kernel implies injectivity by taking differences. Finite direct sums and products have the same coordinates; this proves the first equivalence. For $n=0$, both maps have zero target, and either injectivity condition says $A=0$.

Put $K=\ker\lambda$. Taking $g=1$ in [lem-trf-principal-union-restriction-kernel-localization] identifies $K$ with the kernel of $\mathcal O_X(X)\to\mathcal O_X(U)$, using $X=\operatorname{Spec}A$, $D(1)=X$, and $A_1=A$: the canonical identification $A_1\to A$ sends $a/1^r$ to $a$ and the localization map $A\to A_1$ to the identity. Thus the displayed fractions correspond exactly to $K$ under the same section identification, not merely under an unspecified ring isomorphism. If $\mathcal O_X\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ is injective, the every-open formulation of [def-trf-schematically-dense-open] gives injectivity on $X$, hence $K=0$ and $\lambda$ is injective. Here [def-weil-open-immersion] identifies the structure sheaf of $U$ with the restriction of $\mathcal O_X$. Explicitly, on every open $V$, $(j_*\mathcal O_U)(V)=\mathcal O_U(V\cap U)=\mathcal O_X(V\cap U)$, so these are the same restriction homomorphisms.

Conversely suppose $K=0$. For every $g\in A$, [lem-trf-principal-union-restriction-kernel-localization] identifies the restriction kernel from $D(g)$ to $D(g)\cap U$ with fractions $a/g^r$ having $a\in K$; these are zero since $K=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-localization-away-basic-open](i), the $D(g)$ form a basis. If a section on any open $V$ vanishes on $V\cap U$, its restriction to every $D(g)\subseteq V$ is therefore zero. These basis members cover $V$ (also for non-quasi-compact $V$); all their restricted sections are zero, so sheaf uniqueness makes the section zero. For sections $s,t$ on $V$ with equal restrictions to $V\cap U$, apply this argument to $s-t$ to get $s=t$. Thus restriction is injective on every $V$, precisely sheaf injectivity by [def-trf-schematically-dense-open]. For $n=0$, $K=A$, so this hypothesis forces $A=0$ and all the same kernels vanish. Combining Steps 2--3 with Step 1 proves all three equivalences.
